subject: Performance MAP & concurrency evaluation — Redwood pilot
messages:
From: Patti Wilson <patti@acme.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance MAP & concurrency eval — Redwood pilot

Hi Rishi / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our product team at Acme AI is keen to validate Redwood for a chat-based product that needs consistent TTFT and predictable cost under spiky traffic. High-level targets:
- 95th-percentile generation latency under 300ms for short-turn prompts (<=128 tokens)
- Sustained throughput at 10k tokens/sec with bursts up to 40k tokens/sec for ~30s windows
- Concurrent request fanout expected to reach ~800 concurrent active sessions during peak (apparent QPS/model calls ~1200)

We'd like a Mutual Action Plan that includes a performance benchmarking plan (burst vs steady-state), concrete evaluation harness (traffic shapes, prompt sets), and a recommended close timeline for a 2-week pilot followed by acceptance tests. Also need to capture rate-limit behavior and queueing (how Redwood surfaces backpressure, retry guidance, and billing implications).

Proposed pilot window: first week = integration + smoke tests, second week = full concurrency runs + acceptance. Can you propose a MAP with dates and ownership?

Thanks,
Patti
Patti Wilson
Head of Infrastructure
Acme AI

Acme AI (external)

Hi Patti — great to connect. Attached is a first-pass MAP and evaluation plan (RWD_MAP_draft_20261025.xlsx). High-level summary here so we have a single place to sync: 

1) Objectives & success criteria
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: median <70ms, p95 <300ms for <=128 token prompts during steady-state; for burst windows we allow p95 up to 600ms but require graceful degradation and no system errors.
- Throughput: validate sustained token/sec targets and confirm cost per 1k tokens under proposed batching/quantization settings.
- Concurrency: measure queue depth, request latency distribution, and per-request CPU/GPU utilization during bursts.

2) Test scenarios (detailed in spreadsheet)
- Steady-state: fixed arrival rate at 60% of provisioned capacity for 30m windows.
- Burst: short ramp (5s -> peak) hold for 30s then backoff; repeated 6x to simulate traffic spikes.
- Ramp/soak: progressive concurrency increase to identify throttles and OOM thresholds.

3) Instrumentation & data collection
- Token-level latency, TTFT, GPU load, queueing depth, KV cache hit rates, and failure/error codes.
- We’ll provide a sample prompt suite; Acme to add 10 representative production prompts.

4) Rate-limit & queueing policy testing
- Baseline: default rate-limits in hosted environment.
- Tuning: evaluate soft-window throttles (burst tokens/time) and circuit-breaker thresholds. Neha will own the playbook for how Redwood will apply rate limits and recommended client-side retry/backoff.

5) Ownership & timeline
- Week 1 (integration): Redwood dev + Acme SRE — integration, client SDK config, baseline smoke.
- Week 2 (benchmark): Redwood perf + Acme — steady-state + burst runs, produce acceptance artifact.
- Acceptance test: final 2-hour run with both teams present.

Questions for you: preferred pilot dates (we’ve got Nov 8–21 open), and do you need Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput or will Hosted suffice for the test?

I’ve CC’d Lauren and Neha for sizing/ops. Attaching: RWD_MAP_draft_20261025.xlsx (MAP + test matrix).

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rishi / team —

Looks good. A couple of asks to add into the MAP before we share final:
- Add a decision gate for Dedicated capacity (if Acme wants predictable p95 under 300ms during bursts we should gate on reserving a small Dedicated pool for the acceptance run). Include cost estimate for a 1-week Dedicated reservation.
- Add acceptance criteria that explicitly calls out error-rate limits (e.g., <0.1% 5xx during steady-state).
- Add contact points for on-call escalation during runs (include Marissa as perf lead).

Marissa — please add the short perf-run CSV template and an initial checklist for data ingestion so our perf infra can start templating the runs.

Thanks,
Lauren
VP, Product
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-27T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP & concurrency eval — Redwood pilot

Team — attaching the rate-limit & queueing playbook (rate_limit_playbook.pdf). Highlights to include in MAP: 

- Soft throttles: allow short bursts up to 3x baseline for <=60s windows, then apply token-based backpressure and return 429 with a Retry-After header.
- Circuit breaker: open when sustained 5xx > 0.5% over 1m with per-node isolation.
- Client guidance: exponential backoff with jitter; for interactive apps prefer Hedging at 50ms to reduce tail risk.
- Telemetry hooks: request_id, conn_id, and queue_depth in response headers; we’ll add dashboard links to the MAP.

I’ll own rate-limit tuning during the pilot and coordinate with Acme SRE to iterate thresholds.

—
Neha Kapoor
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Quick upload of initial micro-runs (perf_results_initial.csv attached). Early observations from a sandbox run against a hosted equivalent: 

- Steady-state (45m at 60%): median latency 48ms TTFT, p95 210ms, error-rate 0.02%
- Burst (6x ramps to 1.8k concurrent model calls, ~35k tokens/sec peak, 30s holds): p95 jumped to 740ms for the first two bursts, but subsequent bursts settled to ~420ms after KV-cache warmed; queue_depth peaked at ~240 requests and cleared within 1.2s once burst subsided.
- Observed 429s only during the largest repeated burst when soft-throttle engaged; response included Retry-After and request_id.

Notes: these numbers are from a lightweight sandbox (no Dedicated pool). If Acme opts for a small Dedicated reservation and recommended batching settings (outlined in the MAP), we expect burst p95 to be significantly reduced. Will import full CSV to the shared drive.

Attachments: perf_results_initial.csv (sample rows included)

—
Marissa Cole
Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi / Lauren — and thanks Marissa / Neha for the data. This looks aligned with our expectations. A couple quick confirmations: 
- We want the two-week pilot to start Nov 8 with acceptance test on Nov 19 (we can shorten if Redwood needs).
- We are open to a short Dedicated reservation for the acceptance test — please send pricing and a proposed pool size.
- We’ll add 10 representative prompts to the spreadsheet by EOD Nov 4.

I’ve reviewed the initial perf CSV — the KV-cache effect and queueing behavior are exactly what we expected; good to see Retry-After used rather than silent failures.

Please send a finalized MAP (with the Dedicated cost option) and a 1-paragraph client guidance summary we can share with our app team.

Best,
Patti
